--- title: "Symbolic equilibrium and stability analysis" course-unit: a08-symbolic-analysis status: complete --- ## Analysis, not simulation - The course has simulated, fitted and optimised models. It has not *analysed* one. - Chapter 4 asserted $R_0=\beta c/\gamma$ and the threshold $S/N>1/R_0$, both by hand. - A CAS manipulates expressions, so a result holds for **all** parameter values at once — not just the ones you simulated. ::: {.notes} Frame the appendix as finishing something the foundations chapter started. The distinction to stress: a simulation answers a question about one parameter set, an analysis answers it about the whole parameter space. ::: ## Plain SIR is the wrong model here - Without demography every state with $I=0$ is an equilibrium — a *line*, not a point. - The Jacobian inherits a structural zero eigenvalue; linear stability degenerates. - Add births $\mu N$ and per-capita death $\mu$: population constant, individuals turn over. $$ \dot S = \mu N - \beta c\frac{SI}{N} - \mu S,\quad \dot I = \beta c\frac{SI}{N} - (\gamma+\mu) I,\quad \dot R = \gamma I - \mu R. $$ ::: {.notes} Worth dwelling on. Students often try stability analysis on plain SIR and get confused by the zero eigenvalue. It is not a numerical artefact — it reflects that the model has no endemic state to be stable about. ::: ## Differentiating a vector field exactly ::: {#cell-slide-a10-jacobian .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.julia .cell-code} using Symbolics, LinearAlgebra @variables S I R λ βc γ μ N f = [μ*N - βc*S*I/N - μ*S, βc*S*I/N - γ*I - μ*I, γ*I - μ*R] J_dfe = Symbolics.simplify.(Symbolics.substitute.( Symbolics.jacobian(f, [S, I, R]), (Dict(S => N, I => 0),))) Symbolics.simplify(Symbolics.det(J_dfe - λ*[1 0 0; 0 1 0; 0 0 1])) ``` ::: {#slide-a10-jacobian .cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ::: {.ansi-escaped-output} ```{=html} 
(βc - γ - λ - μ)*((-λ - μ)^2)
``` ::: ::: ::: The polynomial factors on its own: eigenvalues $-\mu$, $-\mu$, and $\beta c-\gamma-\mu$. ::: {.notes} No numbers anywhere. The threshold falls out of the third eigenvalue: stable exactly when βc < γ + μ. That is the foundations result, now derived, and corrected for infectives dying before they recover. ::: ## Routh--Hurwitz: stability without roots - Quadratic $\lambda^2+a_1\lambda+a_2$: $a_1>0$ and $a_2>0$. - Cubic $\lambda^3+a_1\lambda^2+a_2\lambda+a_3$: $a_1>0$, $a_3>0$, $a_1a_2>a_3$. Why this pairs well with a CAS: - the **coefficients** are polynomial in the parameters and come out exactly; - the **roots** of a cubic are unusable as symbolic expressions. ::: {.notes} This is the key methodological point of the session. Do not compute eigenvalues symbolically — compute the characteristic polynomial and test inequalities on its coefficients. ::: ## $R_0$ from a next-generation matrix ::: {#cell-slide-a10-ngm .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.julia .cell-code} Symbolics.simplify(Symbolics.substitute((βc*S/N) / (γ + μ), Dict(S => N))) ``` ::: {#slide-a10-ngm .cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` βc / (γ + μ) ``` ::: ::: $$ R_0=\frac{\beta c}{\gamma+\mu} \xrightarrow{\ \mu\to0\ } \frac{\beta c}{\gamma}. $$ ::: {.notes} Exactly the chapter 4 formula in the limit of no demography. The correction is the probability of dying before recovering. ::: ## What a CAS will not do - `symbolic_solve` cannot solve this system: it is **rational**, not polynomial. - Clearing denominators is a *modelling judgement*, not an algebraic one. - So: derive the equilibrium by hand, let the CAS **verify** it — substitution gives an identically zero residual. - Expression swell kills the approach beyond four or so compartments. ::: {.notes} Resist presenting the CAS as an oracle. The honest workflow is the one used in the chapter: human does the modelling judgement, machine does the mechanical algebra and checks the result. ::: ## Takeaways - Analysis complements simulation: results for **all** parameters, not one set. - Add demography before asking about endemic equilibria. - Routh--Hurwitz decides stability from coefficients — no roots required. - The two equilibria exchange stability at $R_0=1$. - Verify symbolic results numerically; they are only as good as the model. ::: {.notes} Point at the exercises: SEIR gives a genuine cubic where Routh-Hurwitz earns its keep, and SIRS shows when the approach to endemicity becomes oscillatory. :::
